chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.2 Calculation and Billing
chunks.text: The advisory fee is billed quarterly in advance, at one-quarter of the annual fee, based on the aggregate market value of the Family Relationship on the last business day of the preceding calendar quarter. The fee for a partial first quarter is prorated based on the number of days remaining in the quarter. Additions to or withdrawals from a single account exceeding $2,000,000 within a quarter result in a prorated adjustment on the following quarter's invoice. Values used for billing are determined under the Firm's Valuation Policy and may differ from values reported by the custodian, principally for private investments. Because the value of private investments affects the fee, the Firm has an incentive to value them favorably. See "Valuation Risk" in Item 8.3. Fees are deducted from custodial accounts designated by the client under a written authorization delivered to the custodian or, at the client's election, invoiced and payable within 30 days.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.1 Methods of Analysis
chunks.text: The Investment Committee meets monthly. It sets the Firm's capital market assumptions and strategic asset allocation ranges and maintains the approved lists of strategies, managers and funds. For individual securities, the Firm relies principally on fundamental analysis of financial statements and filings, competitive position, balance sheet strength, management and valuation relative to expected cash flows. For fixed income, the Firm analyzes credit quality, concentration, call features, tax status and the yield curve. For third-party managers and private funds, the Firm conducts investment due diligence (strategy, team, track record, portfolio construction and terms) and operational due diligence (governance, valuation practices, service providers, audited financial statements and regulatory history). The Head of Private Investments leads private fund due diligence, and the Investment Committee must approve each fund before any client commits capital.

chunks.text: The Firm implements a strategic asset allocation for each Family Relationship within the ranges set in its IPS, on a tax-aware basis that considers asset location, realization of gains and losses and the use of municipal securities. Principal strategies are: **Core Equity**, a concentrated portfolio of 30 to 45 large and mid capitalization United States companies; **fixed income** portfolios of investment grade municipal, Treasury, agency and corporate bonds; **third-party managers** for international, small capitalization and high yield mandates; **private markets** funds and co-investments in private equity, venture capital, private credit and real estate, subscribed for in the name of each investing client; and **concentrated position strategies**, including staged sales, charitable transfers, exchange funds and collars implemented at Corvedale Clay Securities, LLC.

Diversification does not eliminate market risk. **Interest Rate and Credit Risk.** Fixed income securities decline in value when interest rates rise. Issuers may fail to pay interest or principal, and downgrades may reduce market value before any default. Municipal securities are also affected by the fiscal condition of the issuer and by changes in tax law. **Equity Concentration Risk.** The Core Equity strategy holds a limited number of issuers. A decline in a single holding has a larger effect than it would on a broadly diversified portfolio. Many families also hold legacy positions in a single security, often with a low tax basis, which the family may elect to retain for tax, control or personal reasons. **Liquidity and Capital Call Risk.** Private funds and co-investments are illiquid, generally cannot be redeemed, require the general partner's consent to transfer and have terms of ten years or longer. Funds call committed capital over several years. A client that fails to meet a capital call may forfeit all or part of its interest. **Valuation Risk.** Private investments are valued under the Firm's Valuation Policy, principally on the basis of values reported by fund sponsors, which are estimates and are often reported months after the valuation date. Each account receives the average price and bears its own transaction costs. Aggregated orders are allocated under a written pre-allocation prepared before the order is placed, and partially filled orders are allocated pro rata. Opportunities of limited capacity in private funds and co-investments are allocated under written procedures adopted by the Investment Committee that consider each family's eligibility, suitability and IPS target allocation.

chunks.section: Preamble
chunks.text: # Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual **Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC** Version 2026.1, effective January 15, 2026 Adopted by the Management Committee on January 13, 2026 > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC, Quenby Holt Trust Company and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Manual sets out the written policies and procedures that Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC (the "Firm") has adopted under Rule 206(4)-7 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to prevent violations of the Advisers Act and the rules thereunder, together with the Firm's Code of Ethics under Rule 204A-1. The Manual is supplemented by the Firm's Valuation Policy and Business Continuity Plan, each of which is incorporated by reference. Where this Manual is more restrictive than applicable law, the Manual governs the conduct of Supervised Persons.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.2 Persons Covered
chunks.text: This Manual applies to all members, officers and employees of the Firm, and to any other person who provides investment advice on behalf of the Firm and is subject to its supervision and control (each, a "Supervised Person"). Officers and employees of Quenby Holt Trust Company ("QHTC") who have access to nonpublic information regarding the Firm's client transactions or holdings are Supervised Persons for purposes of Sections 3, 4, 5 and 7. Temporary staff and consultants with access to Firm systems are subject to Sections 7, 11, 12 and 14 and must sign the Firm's confidentiality undertaking before access is granted.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.3 Definitions
chunks.text: "Access Person" means any Supervised Person who has access to nonpublic information regarding any client's purchase or sale of securities or the portfolio holdings of any client, or who is involved in making securities recommendations to clients. All Firm employees are designated Access Persons. "Reportable Account" means any account in which an Access Person has a direct or indirect beneficial interest and that holds or can hold Reportable Securities, including accounts of the Access Person's spouse, domestic partner, minor children and any other relative sharing the same household. "Reportable Security" has the meaning given in Rule 204A-1 and excludes direct obligations of the United States government, bankers' acceptances, bank certificates of deposit, commercial paper, high quality short-term debt instruments, money market fund shares and shares of open-end funds that are not advised by the Firm. "Family Relationship" means all accounts of a client family aggregated under a single investment management agreement. "Compliance System" means the Tollard Compliance Suite, through which pre-clearance requests, holdings and transaction reports, gifts and entertainment logs, political contribution requests and attestations are submitted and retained.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.1 Designation
chunks.text: The Management Committee has designated Theresa L. Vannoy as Chief Compliance Officer of the Firm (the "CCO"). The CCO reports directly to the Managing Partner and has unrestricted access to the Management Committee. The CCO may delegate specific tasks to the Compliance Manager, Nadia R. Kessling, but remains responsible for the administration of the compliance program. The designation of any successor CCO requires action of the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.2 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The CCO is responsible for administering this Manual and the Code of Ethics; maintaining the Restricted List, Watch List and Client-Affiliated Issuer List; approving pre-clearance requests, gifts and entertainment above stated thresholds, political contributions and outside activities; reviewing and approving advertisements; overseeing the Firm's cybersecurity and privacy programs jointly with the Information Security Officer; conducting the annual review described in Section 15; delivering compliance training; and coordinating responses to regulatory inquiries.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.3 Authority and Resources
chunks.text: The CCO has full authority to access all books, records, systems and personnel of the Firm, to require corrective action, and to escalate any matter to the Management Committee. The CCO's compensation is set by the Managing Partner and is not tied to the Firm's assets under management or to the investment performance of any account. The CCO may engage outside counsel or compliance consultants, subject to the budget approved annually by the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.4 Coordination with Quenby Holt Trust Company
chunks.text: QHTC maintains a separate compliance program under the South Dakota trust company laws and the Bank Secrecy Act, administered by its Trust Compliance and BSA Officer, Lorna Keplinger, who reports to the QHTC board of directors. The CCO and the Trust Compliance and BSA Officer meet at least quarterly to review matters affecting both entities, including conflicts arising from QHTC's appointment as trustee of trusts advised by the Firm, shared personnel and shared systems. Each maintains a written record of those meetings.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.1 Standards of Business Conduct
chunks.text: The Firm is a fiduciary to each of its clients. Supervised Persons must place the interests of clients ahead of their own and the Firm's, must not take inappropriate advantage of their positions, must avoid or disclose conflicts of interest, and must comply with applicable federal securities laws. Supervised Persons must keep confidential all information about client families, including their holdings, transactions, family relationships, estate plans and business interests, and may use that information only to serve the family.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.2 Acknowledgment
chunks.text: Each Supervised Person must acknowledge in writing, through the Compliance System, receipt of the Code and this Manual upon hire, upon each amendment and annually.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.3 Reporting Violations
chunks.text: Supervised Persons must report promptly to the CCO any violation or apparent violation of the Code or this Manual of which they become aware, including violations by others. If the matter involves the CCO, the report is made to the Managing Partner. Reports may be made anonymously in writing. The Firm prohibits retaliation against any person who makes a report in good faith.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.4 Sanctions
chunks.text: Violations may result in a written warning, disgorgement of profits, reversal of trades at the Access Person's expense, suspension of personal trading privileges, reduction of discretionary compensation, suspension or termination of employment, and referral to regulatory authorities. Disgorged amounts are donated to a charity selected by the CCO. The CCO records each violation and sanction in the Compliance System and reports material violations to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.1 Reportable Accounts
chunks.text: Each Access Person must disclose every Reportable Account and must arrange for the broker-dealer or custodian to deliver duplicate statements or an electronic data feed to the Compliance System. A Reportable Account over which the Access Person has no direct or indirect influence or control, such as a discretionary account managed by an unaffiliated adviser, may be exempted from pre-clearance by the CCO upon receipt of a written certification from the account manager, but remains subject to reporting.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.2 Pre-Clearance
chunks.text: Except as provided in Section 4.3, an Access Person must obtain pre-clearance through the Compliance System before effecting any transaction in a Reportable Security, including exchange-traded funds and closed-end funds. Pre-clearance requests are approved by the CCO or the Compliance Manager. The CCO's own requests are approved by the Chief Financial Officer. Pre-clearance approval is valid only for the business day on which it is granted. Orders not executed by the close of that business day must be resubmitted. Good-until-cancelled and other standing orders are not permitted unless pre-cleared each day on which they may execute. The CCO or Compliance Manager will deny a request if the security is on the Restricted List, if there is an open or pending order for the security in any client account, or if the transaction would violate Section 4.4 or 4.5.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.3 De Minimis Exemption
chunks.text: Transactions in the equity securities of an issuer with a market capitalization of at least $10 billion are exempt from pre-clearance where the Access Person's aggregate transactions in that issuer do not exceed $25,000 in any 30 calendar day period. Transactions relying on this exemption remain subject to reporting, to the holding period in Section 4.5, and to the prohibitions in Sections 4.4 and 7. The exemption is not available for securities on the Restricted List or the Client-Affiliated Issuer List. Broad-based index exchange-traded funds designated by the CCO on the Compliance System are also exempt from pre-clearance but remain reportable.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.4 Prohibited and Restricted Transactions
chunks.text: Access Persons may not: 1. acquire any security in an initial public offering; 2. acquire any security in a limited offering, including a private fund or co-investment, without the prior written approval of the CCO, which will be granted for a private fund or co-investment recommended to clients only after the allocations of all eligible Family Relationships have been satisfied; 3. trade in any security while in possession of material nonpublic information about the issuer; 4. trade in any security on the Restricted List; 5. purchase or sell options on, or sell short, any security held in the Core Equity strategy; or 6. trade ahead of, or on the basis of knowledge of, any client order.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.5 Holding Period and Blackout Periods
chunks.text: Reportable Securities acquired by an Access Person must be held for at least 30 calendar days. The CCO may grant exceptions in cases of hardship, provided the security has not been purchased or sold for a client account in the preceding 30 days. Profits realized in violation of the holding period are disgorged. No Access Person may trade a security within three business days before or after a transaction in that security for the Core Equity strategy. Transactions in securities held only in sleeves managed by third-party managers are not subject to the blackout period.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.6 Holdings and Transaction Reports
chunks.text: Each Access Person must submit through the Compliance System: an initial holdings report within 10 days after becoming an Access Person, with information current as of a date not more than 45 days before the report; an annual holdings report no later than February 14 of each year, with information current as of December 31 of the prior year; and a quarterly transaction report no later than 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter, covering every transaction in a Reportable Security during the quarter. Transactions reported through an electronic data feed satisfy the quarterly transaction report requirement for the covered account if the Access Person confirms the completeness of the feed in the Compliance System within the same deadline.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.7 Review of Personal Trading
chunks.text: The Compliance Manager reviews all holdings and transaction reports and compares personal transactions with client trading, the Restricted List and the Client-Affiliated Issuer List. The CCO's reports are reviewed by the Chief Financial Officer. Exceptions are documented in the Compliance System and escalated to the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.1 General Principles
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may not give or accept any gift, entertainment or other benefit that could reasonably be expected to influence the recipient's business judgment or to create an obligation. Gifts of cash or cash equivalents, including gift cards, are prohibited regardless of amount. Soliciting gifts or entertainment is prohibited.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.2 Gifts
chunks.text: No Supervised Person may give or accept gifts with an aggregate value exceeding $250 per source or recipient per calendar year without the prior written approval of the CCO. Gifts of nominal value bearing a company logo and customary holiday food items shared with the office are excluded from the aggregate. All gifts given or received, other than excluded items, must be logged in the Compliance System within five business days.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.3 Business Entertainment
chunks.text: Business entertainment is permitted where the provider attends and the entertainment is reasonable in frequency and value. Entertainment with a value exceeding $500 per person per event requires the prior approval of the CCO. Supervised Persons may not accept travel or lodging paid for by a third-party manager, fund sponsor or broker-dealer. The Firm pays its own travel costs for manager due diligence visits.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.4 Gifts from Client Families
chunks.text: Client families frequently give gifts to Firm personnel on holidays and family occasions. Such gifts are subject to Section 5.2. A gift from a client family that exceeds the threshold may be accepted only with the CCO's written approval, which will consider whether the gift could be perceived as influencing the treatment of that family relative to others. Supervised Persons may not accept bequests or be named as beneficiaries under any client's estate plan, other than a relative's.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.1 Regulatory Framework
chunks.text: Rule 206(4)-5 under the Advisers Act prohibits an adviser from providing advisory services for compensation to a government entity within two years after a contribution to certain officials of that entity by the adviser or any of its covered associates. The Firm does not currently advise any government entity, but applies this Section so that no contribution restricts the Firm's future business.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.2 Pre-Clearance of Contributions
chunks.text: Every Supervised Person must obtain the CCO's pre-clearance through the Compliance System before making any contribution to, or soliciting or coordinating contributions for, a state or local official, a candidate for state or local office, a state or local political party, or a political action committee. Pre-clearance is also required for contributions to a candidate for federal office who currently holds state or local office. Contributions within the de minimis amounts permitted by the rule ($350 per election for a candidate for whom the contributor is entitled to vote and $150 per election otherwise) still require pre-clearance.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.3 New Employees
chunks.text: Each new Supervised Person must disclose all contributions described in Section 6.2 made during the two years before hire, or the six months before hire for a person who will not solicit clients, so that the CCO can determine whether any restriction applies.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.4 Prohibited Conduct
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may not make contributions through spouses, family members, entities or other persons to avoid this Section, may not bundle contributions, and may not use Firm resources for political activity.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.1 Policy
chunks.text: No Supervised Person may trade, for any client or personal account, in a security while in possession of material nonpublic information ("MNPI") about the issuer, or communicate MNPI to others in violation of law. Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important in making an investment decision, and nonpublic until it has been broadly disseminated. Client families are frequently founders, directors and senior officers of public companies, and Supervised Persons must treat information obtained from families about those companies as presumptively MNPI.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.2 Restricted List and Watch List
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a Restricted List of issuers about which the Firm or a Supervised Person may possess MNPI, and a Watch List of issuers under heightened review. No trade in a Restricted List issuer may be effected for any client account or Reportable Account while the issuer remains on the list. The Watch List is confidential to the compliance department.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.3 Client-Affiliated Issuers
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a Client-Affiliated Issuer List of public companies of which a member of a client family is an officer, director or beneficial owner of 10% or more of any class of equity securities. No transaction in a security of an issuer on the Client-Affiliated Issuer List may be effected for any client account or Reportable Account without the prior approval of the CCO. For a transaction in the affiliated family member's own accounts, the CCO will also require written confirmation from the family member, or the issuer's general counsel, that the transaction is permitted under the issuer's trading window or is made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, and that any required Rule 144 or Section 16 filings will be made.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.4 Outside Board Service
chunks.text: No Supervised Person may serve as a director of a public company without the prior approval of the Management Committee. The CCO places the issuer of any approved directorship on the Restricted List.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.5 Escalation
chunks.text: A Supervised Person who believes he or she may have received MNPI must immediately notify the CCO and refrain from trading and from discussing the information with anyone else. The CCO will determine whether to add the issuer to the Restricted List and will document the determination.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS REVIEW > 8.1 Scope
chunks.text: This Section applies to every advertisement within the meaning of Rule 206(4)-1, including presentations to prospective families, the Firm's website, newsletters, social media content and any communication that offers the Firm's advisory services to more than one person.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS REVIEW > 8.2 Review and Approval
chunks.text: Every advertisement must be approved in writing by the CCO before first use. The Compliance Manager may approve advertisements that contain no performance information. Approvals and final versions are retained in the Compliance System.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS REVIEW > 8.3 Performance Presentation
chunks.text: Any presentation of gross performance must be accompanied by net performance calculated with equal prominence over the same periods. Performance for any portfolio must be presented for one-, five- and ten-year periods, or since inception if shorter. The Firm does not use hypothetical or extracted performance in advertisements. Composite performance of the Core Equity strategy is calculated by the Controller and reviewed by the CCO before each use.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS REVIEW > 8.4 Testimonials, Endorsements and Third-Party Ratings
chunks.text: The Firm does not use testimonials of client families in any advertisement. Endorsements and third-party ratings may be used only with the prior approval of the CCO and the disclosures required by Rule 206(4)-1.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS REVIEW > 8.5 Social Media
chunks.text: Supervised Persons may share Firm content approved under Section 8.2 on professional networking sites but may not create content describing the Firm's services, investment views or client matters.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.1 Aggregation
chunks.text: Orders for the same security for more than one account may be aggregated when the portfolio manager determines that aggregation is consistent with best execution and with the IPS of each account, and that no account will be systematically disadvantaged. Before an aggregated order is placed, the portfolio manager records a pre-allocation specifying the participating accounts and the amount for each.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.2 Allocation of Aggregated Orders
chunks.text: Each account participating in an aggregated order receives the average execution price and bears its own custodial transaction charges. A partially filled order is allocated pro rata in proportion to the pre-allocation, except that the portfolio manager may allocate to fewer accounts where a pro rata allocation would give an account a position too small to be meaningful, provided the basis is documented. Accounts of Access Persons included in an aggregated order receive allocations only after client accounts are filled in full.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.3 Deviations
chunks.text: Any allocation that departs from the pre-allocation, other than as permitted in Section 9.2, requires the approval of the CCO before the end of the trade date, with a written explanation retained in the order management system.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.4 Limited Private Investment Opportunities
chunks.text: Private funds with limited capacity and co-investment opportunities are allocated as follows. The Head of Private Investments presents the opportunity to the Investment Committee, which first determines which Family Relationships are eligible, taking into account investor qualification status, suitability, liquidity, concentration and the IPS. Where aggregate eligible demand exceeds available capacity, the Investment Committee allocates the opportunity among eligible Family Relationships pro rata in proportion to each Family Relationship's shortfall relative to the private markets target allocation in its Investment Policy Statement, subject to a minimum allocation of $250,000 per Family Relationship. The Head of Private Investments documents the eligibility determination and the allocation, and the CCO reviews each allocation before commitments are submitted. Supervised Persons may participate only after the demand of all eligible Family Relationships has been satisfied.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE AGGREGATION AND ALLOCATION > 9.5 Cross Trades and Intra-Family Transfers
chunks.text: Cross trades between accounts of different Family Relationships are prohibited. Transfers between accounts within the same Family Relationship are permitted at the custodian's closing price, without commission, with the prior approval of the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.1 Duty
chunks.text: The Firm seeks to execute client transactions so that the total cost or proceeds in each transaction is the most favorable under the circumstances, considering price, commission, speed and likelihood of execution, market impact, the broker-dealer's financial condition and the quality of its services.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.2 Trade Oversight Committee
chunks.text: The Trade Oversight Committee, consisting of the Chief Investment Officer, the Director of Operations and the CCO, meets semi-annually, in January and July, to review execution quality. The review covers custodian execution quality reports, commission and markup levels on fixed income transactions compared with contemporaneous market data, the performance of each approved broker-dealer and trade errors, and, at the July meeting, the Firm's recommendation of custodians. The Committee's conclusions and any resulting changes are recorded in minutes retained by the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.3 Approved Broker-Dealers; No Soft Dollars
chunks.text: Transactions may be executed only through broker-dealers on the approved list maintained by the Trade Oversight Committee. The Firm does not accept research or other products or services in exchange for client brokerage.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.1 Program and Responsibility
chunks.text: The Firm maintains a written information security program designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of client information and Firm systems. Ingrid P. Solheim, Director of Technology and Information Security, serves as Information Security Officer (the "ISO") and reports on the program to the Management Committee at least quarterly.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.2 Access Controls
chunks.text: Multi-factor authentication is required for email, remote access, the reporting platform and every custodian portal. Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and is reviewed quarterly by the ISO with each department head. Access of a departing employee is disabled no later than the end of the employee's last day. Firm laptops and mobile devices are encrypted and managed centrally.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.3 Monitoring and Managed Services
chunks.text: Pellow Stack IT, LLC provides managed information technology services, including endpoint management and patching. Critical security patches are applied within 14 days of release. Northgale Security Operations, Inc. provides 24-hour monitoring of the Firm's endpoints, email and network through a managed detection and response service and escalates alerts to the ISO in accordance with agreed severity levels.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.4 Vulnerability Management and Penetration Testing
chunks.text: Northgale Security Operations, Inc. performs vulnerability scans of the Firm's external and internal networks quarterly. Ostler Vane Security Testing, LLC performs an external penetration test annually, and its findings are reported to the Management Committee with a remediation plan and target dates tracked by the ISO. The ISO conducts phishing simulations quarterly, and employees who fail a simulation complete supplemental training.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.5 Vendor Oversight
chunks.text: Before engaging any vendor that will store or access client information, and annually for each critical vendor thereafter, the ISO obtains and reviews the vendor's most recent SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent and its incident notification commitments. Contracts with such vendors must require notice to the Firm as soon as possible, and in any event within 72 hours, after the vendor becomes aware of a breach affecting the Firm's customer information.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.6 Incident Response
chunks.text: Any Supervised Person who suspects a cybersecurity incident must report it immediately to the ISO. The ISO acts as Incident Response Lead and notifies the CCO within one hour of determining that an incident may involve client information or funds. Northgale Security Operations, Inc. will be engaged to perform containment, forensic investigation and eradication. The ISO and CCO will engage the outside breach counsel designated in the Business Continuity Plan and ask the Chief Financial Officer to notify the Firm's cyber liability insurer. Where client accounts may be affected, the Director of Operations will ask the relevant custodian to apply heightened review to disbursements. The CCO determines, with counsel, whether notice to clients, regulators or law enforcement is required.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.7 Cyber Liability Insurance
chunks.text: The Firm maintains a cyber liability insurance policy covering incident response costs, business interruption, funds transfer fraud and third-party liability. The Chief Financial Officer reviews the adequacy of coverage annually at renewal with the ISO and the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.8 Disbursement and Wire Controls
chunks.text: Every request to transfer funds to a third party, or to change standing payment instructions, must be confirmed by a telephone call to the client at a number on file, not a number supplied in the request. Disbursements above $100,000 require approval by two authorized employees. Requests received only by email or text are never executed without that call.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.1 Regulation S-P
chunks.text: The Firm protects nonpublic personal information of clients in accordance with Regulation S-P. The Firm delivers its privacy notice at the inception of each client relationship. Because the Firm shares nonpublic personal information only as permitted by the exceptions in Regulation S-P and has not changed its policies, it is not required to deliver an annual privacy notice.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.2 Sharing of Information
chunks.text: The Firm shares nonpublic personal information with QHTC, custodians, the reporting platform, the family's attorneys and accountants and other service providers only as needed to provide services, and does not share information with any non-affiliated third party for marketing purposes.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.3 Family Information Authorizations
chunks.text: Information about one family member's accounts is shared with another family member only in accordance with a written Family Information Authorization signed by the account owner or trustee, which records which family members may receive which information. Relationship Leads must confirm the authorization before sharing any account information within a family.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.4 Customer Notification
chunks.text: If sensitive customer information has been, or is reasonably likely to have been, accessed or used without authorization, the Firm will notify each affected individual as soon as practicable, and not later than 30 days after becoming aware of the incident, unless the CCO determines, after a reasonable investigation, that the information has not been and is not reasonably likely to be used in a manner that would result in substantial harm or inconvenience.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 12. PRIVACY OF CLIENT INFORMATION > 12.5 Disposal
chunks.text: Records containing client information are disposed of by shredding or secure electronic destruction. Vendors that dispose of Firm records must certify destruction in writing.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 13. BOOKS AND RECORDS > 13.1 Retention Period
chunks.text: The Firm retains all books and records required by Rule 204-2 for seven years from the end of the fiscal year during which the last entry was made on the record, the first two years in an appropriate office of the Firm. Partnership and organizational documents of the Firm are retained for the life of the Firm and for three years after its termination.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 13. BOOKS AND RECORDS > 13.2 Electronic Storage
chunks.text: Email, collaboration platform messages and business text messages are captured and retained by Arcwell Archive Services, Inc. in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format, indexed and searchable. Other electronic records are retained on Firm systems with access controls and backups described in the Business Continuity Plan. The Firm must be able to produce any record promptly upon request.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 13. BOOKS AND RECORDS > 13.3 Trust Company Records
chunks.text: QHTC retains its trust records in accordance with South Dakota law and its own policies. Where a record is required of both the Firm and QHTC, each entity retains its own copy.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.1 Approved Channels
chunks.text: Business communications must be conducted only through the Firm's email system, the Firm's collaboration platform and the Firm-issued mobile messaging application, each of which is archived by Arcwell Archive Services, Inc. Communications with families through the reporting portal are retained by the portal provider and captured by the Firm.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.2 Prohibited Channels and Off-Channel Messages
chunks.text: Personal email, personal text messaging and consumer messaging applications may not be used for Firm business. If a client or other person sends a business communication to a Supervised Person through an unapproved channel, the Supervised Person must respond only through an approved channel and must forward the message to the Firm's archive within one business day.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 14. ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS > 14.3 Surveillance
chunks.text: The Compliance Manager reviews messages flagged by lexicon-based surveillance weekly and reviews a random sample of at least 50 messages each month. Reviews and escalations are documented in the archive.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 15. ANNUAL REVIEW > 15.1 Requirement
chunks.text: Rule 206(4)-7 requires the Firm to review, no less frequently than annually, the adequacy of its policies and procedures and the effectiveness of their implementation.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 15. ANNUAL REVIEW > 15.2 Conduct and Reporting
chunks.text: The CCO conducts the annual review with the assistance of Hethersett Compliance Advisors, LLC. The review covers the prior calendar year and includes forensic testing of personal trading, allocation, fee calculations, custody arrangements, marketing and cybersecurity controls, and consideration of any compliance matters, changes in the Firm's business and changes in applicable law. The CCO delivers a written report of its findings to the Management Committee no later than April 30 of each year. The Management Committee documents its response to each recommendation.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 15. ANNUAL REVIEW > 15.3 Interim Reviews
chunks.text: The CCO conducts an interim review upon any significant compliance event, change in business, or change in law, and amends this Manual as necessary. Amendments are approved by the Management Committee and communicated to Supervised Persons in writing.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 16. TRAINING AND ATTESTATIONS > 16.1 Training
chunks.text: Each new Supervised Person must complete compliance training covering this Manual and the Code of Ethics within 30 days after the start of employment. All Supervised Persons must complete annual compliance training, delivered in the fourth quarter, which addresses changes in the Manual and law, the prior year's compliance matters and cybersecurity.

chunks.label: Compliance Policies and Procedures Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 16. TRAINING AND ATTESTATIONS > 16.2 Attestations
chunks.text: Each Supervised Person must certify through the Compliance System, by January 31 of each year, that he or she has read and complied with this Manual and the Code of Ethics during the prior year, has disclosed all Reportable Accounts and outside activities, and has reported all gifts, entertainment and political contributions required to be reported.

chunks.section: Preamble
chunks.text: # Valuation Policy **Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC** Version 4.0, adopted February 10, 2026 Approved by the Management Committee > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC, Quenby Holt Trust Company and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Policy establishes the methods and controls by which Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC (the "Firm") values client holdings for consolidated client reporting and for the calculation of advisory fees. Because the Firm's advisory fee is based on the value of each Family Relationship, including private investments, the Firm has an interest in higher valuations. This Policy is designed to ensure that values are determined consistently, from independent sources wherever available, and with oversight by persons who do not make investment decisions for clients.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.2 Scope
chunks.text: This Policy applies to all assets included in regulatory assets under management and to reporting-only assets included in consolidated reports. The account statements issued by qualified custodians remain the official record of client holdings for custody purposes. Quenby Holt Trust Company ("QHTC") values trust assets for fiduciary accountings under its own procedures, which rely on values determined under this Policy for assets advised by the Firm.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.1 Composition
chunks.text: The Valuation Committee (the "Committee") consists of four voting members: the Chief Financial Officer, the Controller, the Director of Operations and the President of Quenby Holt Trust Company. The Chief Investment Officer, the Head of Private Investments and the Chief Compliance Officer attend as non-voting members. Non-voting members may present information and recommendations but may not vote, and the Head of Private Investments is excused from deliberation on any position for which he or she prepared the valuation recommendation.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.2 Quorum and Voting
chunks.text: A quorum consists of three voting members, one of whom must be the Chief Financial Officer or the Controller. Determinations are made by a majority of the voting members present. A voting member who has a personal interest in a position, including through a Reportable Account or a family relationship with the issuer, must disclose the interest and abstain.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.3 Meetings
chunks.text: The Committee meets quarterly, within 15 business days after the end of each calendar quarter, to approve the valuations of all Level 3 positions as of the quarter end and to review the reports described in Sections 5 through 7. The Chief Financial Officer or the Controller may call a special meeting at any time, including upon a significant market event, a credit event affecting a held issuer, or the receipt of information suggesting that a reported value is unreliable. Minutes of every meeting are kept by the Controller and retained with the supporting materials.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.4 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The Committee is responsible for approving pricing sources and the hierarchy in Section 3; approving the valuation of each Level 3 position; reviewing price challenges, overrides and stale price reports; reviewing back-testing results; engaging and overseeing the independent valuation firm; and reviewing this Policy annually and recommending amendments to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.1 Hierarchy
chunks.text: Assets are valued using the first available source in the following order: (a) a price from an approved pricing vendor under Sections 3.2 and 3.3; (b) the price provided by the qualified custodian; (c) a broker quotation obtained by Operations from a broker-dealer that is not the counterparty to a pending client transaction; and (d) fair value determined under Section 4. Assets are classified within the fair value hierarchy of ASC 820 (Level 1, Level 2 or Level 3) for reporting purposes.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.2 Listed Securities
chunks.text: Equity securities, exchange-traded funds, closed-end funds and listed options traded on a national securities exchange are valued at the official closing price on the primary exchange, or, if no trade occurred, the mean of the closing bid and ask prices, as supplied by Ostrander Valuation Data, Inc. Securities traded principally on a non-United States exchange are valued at the closing price on that exchange converted to United States dollars at the 4:00 p.m. Eastern time exchange rate supplied by the same vendor.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.3 Fixed Income
chunks.text: For fixed income securities, including municipal, Treasury, agency, corporate and securitized debt, Ostrander Valuation Data, Inc. is the primary pricing source and supplies evaluated bid prices. Kilbride Evaluated Pricing LLC serves as the secondary source and is used when Ostrander does not price a security, when a challenge to an Ostrander price under Section 5 remains unresolved, or when the Controller determines that the Ostrander price is unreliable. Use of the secondary source for any security for more than five consecutive business days is reported to the Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.4 Funds and Cash
chunks.text: Open-end mutual funds and money market funds are valued at the net asset value published by the fund. Cash and bank deposits are valued at their balances as reported by the custodian or depository bank. Separately managed account sleeves of third-party managers are valued using the sources in Sections 3.2 and 3.3, and differences from the manager's own valuations above the tolerances in Section 5.1 are investigated.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.5 Custodian Price Comparison
chunks.text: Each business day Operations compares vendor prices for all positions with the prices reported by Norrell Bay Trust & Custody, N.A. and Corvedale Clay Securities, LLC. The comparison is the basis for the tolerance checks in Section 5.1.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRIVATE INVESTMENTS AND LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.1 Classification
chunks.text: Private investments include interests in private funds, co-investments, direct investments in private companies, and interests in real estate and operating businesses held for families within the Firm's management authority. Where no observable input is available, the investment is classified as Level 3.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRIVATE INVESTMENTS AND LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.2 Interests in Private Funds
chunks.text: Interests in private funds are valued at the most recent net asset value reported by the general partner or fund administrator, adjusted for capital calls and distributions occurring after the reporting date. The Firm does not apply its own adjustments to a reported net asset value unless the Committee determines that the reported value does not reflect fair value, for example because of a known subsequent event, a reported value that is not based on fair value principles, or a qualified audit opinion. Any such adjustment requires the approval of the Committee and is disclosed in client reports.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRIVATE INVESTMENTS AND LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.3 Direct Private Investments
chunks.text: Co-investments and direct investments in private companies are valued at fair value using one or more of the following methods, applied consistently from period to period: 1. **Calibration to transaction price.** At acquisition, the investment is valued at cost, and the inputs to subsequent valuations are calibrated to the transaction. 2. **Market approach.** Enterprise value is estimated by applying multiples of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or other appropriate metrics, derived from comparable public companies and precedent transactions, adjusted for differences in size, growth and margins. 3. **Income approach.** Enterprise value is estimated by discounting projected cash flows at a rate reflecting the risk of the investment. 4. **Recent transactions.** A subsequent financing round or secondary sale involving unrelated parties at arm's length is considered, weighted according to the size of the transaction and the rights of the securities involved. Equity value is allocated among classes of securities in accordance with their rights and preferences. A discount for lack of marketability, generally within a range of 10% to 30%, is applied where the Firm's clients hold minority interests without liquidity rights. The selected method, key inputs and the rationale for any change in method are documented in the valuation memorandum for each position.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRIVATE INVESTMENTS AND LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.4 Real Estate and Operating Company Interests
chunks.text: Directly held real estate within the Firm's management authority is valued on the basis of an independent appraisal obtained at least every three years, updated in intervening quarters for capital expenditures, material changes in occupancy and changes in capitalization rates observed in the relevant market. Interests in family operating companies that are reporting-only assets are reported at values supplied by the family and are labeled as such in client reports; they are not included in the fee base except at the reporting-only rate.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PRIVATE INVESTMENTS AND LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.5 Documentation
chunks.text: For every Level 3 position, the Controller maintains a valuation memorandum containing the valuation as of each quarter end, the method and inputs used, the sources of information, a comparison to the prior valuation with an explanation of significant changes, and the Committee's approval.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.1 Tolerance Checks
chunks.text: A vendor price that differs from the custodian's price by more than 2% for an equity security or exchange-traded fund, or by more than 1% of price for a fixed income security, is reported on the daily exception report. Operations also reports any fixed income price that moves more than 3% from the prior business day without a corresponding movement in comparable securities.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.2 Price Challenges
chunks.text: Operations submits a challenge to the relevant vendor within one business day of identifying an exception that it cannot resolve by reference to market information, providing the evidence supporting an alternative price. The challenge and the vendor's response are logged. If the vendor maintains its price after review, Operations may use the vendor price or propose an override under Section 5.3.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.3 Overrides
chunks.text: If a challenge remains unresolved after two business days, or if Operations or the Controller determines that no vendor or custodian price reflects fair value, an override price may be used. Any override of a price supplied by a pricing source must be approved in advance by the Chief Investment Officer, on the basis of a written recommendation from the Controller stating the proposed price, the reason for the override and the supporting evidence. Overrides remain in effect only until a reliable vendor price becomes available and are reviewed at every business day's exception review.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.4 Override Log
chunks.text: The Controller maintains a log of all overrides, recording the security, the vendor price, the override price, the approver, the dates of approval and removal, and the market value effect on each affected Family Relationship. The log is reported to the Committee at each meeting and reviewed by the Chief Compliance Officer as part of the annual review.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.1 Daily Stale Price Report
chunks.text: Operations produces a daily stale price report that flags any security whose price has not changed for five consecutive business days. Operations investigates each flagged security and documents whether the unchanged price reflects actual market conditions, such as an illiquid municipal issue, or a failure of the pricing feed. A security whose price has not changed for ten consecutive business days is escalated to the Valuation Committee, which determines whether to continue using the price, obtain a broker quotation, or apply a fair value under Section 4.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.2 Private Fund Reporting Lag
chunks.text: Operations flags any private fund interest for which the most recent reported net asset value is dated more than 120 days before the valuation date. The Head of Private Investments contacts the general partner for an updated value, and the Committee considers at its next meeting whether an adjustment under Section 4.2 is warranted.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. BACK-TESTING > 7.1 Quarterly Back-Testing
chunks.text: Each quarter, the Controller compares the prices used for positions sold during the quarter with the actual sale prices, and compares the prior quarter-end values of private fund interests with the net asset values subsequently reported by the general partners for the same date. Any variance greater than 5% is investigated and explained in the back-testing report delivered to the Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. BACK-TESTING > 7.2 Level 3 Realization Review
chunks.text: Upon the realization of any direct Level 3 position, the Controller compares the realized proceeds with the valuations reported over the preceding four quarters and presents the comparison to the Committee, which considers whether the methods or inputs used for similar positions should be revised.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.1 Independent Valuation Firm
chunks.text: Tessier Arkwright Valuation Group performs an independent valuation of each direct Level 3 position with a carrying value above $10,000,000 at least annually, and of every other direct Level 3 position at least once every three years. The independent valuation firm reports to the Committee, and its engagement is approved by the Committee rather than by the investment team. Where the Firm's valuation of a position differs from the independent valuation by more than 10%, the Committee documents the reasons for the value it adopts.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.2 Annual Policy Review
chunks.text: The Committee reviews this Policy at least annually, with the participation of the Chief Compliance Officer, and recommends any amendments to the Management Committee for approval. The Chief Compliance Officer also tests the application of this Policy to advisory fee calculations as part of the annual review of the compliance program.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026

chunks.text: This Business Continuity Plan (the "Plan") describes how Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC (the "Firm") will continue to meet its obligations to client families, including trading, cash management, bill payment, capital call funding and reporting, during and after a significant business disruption. Solheim, Director of Technology and Information Security, serves as alternate BCP Coordinator. chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND PLAN OWNERSHIP > 1.3 Approval and Review
chunks.text: The Management Committee approves the Plan at least annually and upon any material change in the Firm's operations, locations or critical vendors. The Chief Compliance Officer reviews the Plan as part of the annual review of the compliance program.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. DECLARATION AND ESCALATION > 2.1 Disruption Scenarios
chunks.text: The Plan addresses loss of access to the principal office (including fire, severe weather, utility failure and civil disturbance); loss of systems or data (including ransomware and other cyber incidents); failure of a critical vendor; a pandemic or other public health event that reduces available staff; and a regional disruption affecting the Minneapolis area.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. DECLARATION AND ESCALATION > 2.2 Declaration Authority
chunks.text: A business disruption may be declared by the Managing Partner or, if she is unavailable, by the Chief Financial Officer or, if neither is available, by the BCP Coordinator. The person declaring records the time of declaration, which starts the recovery time objectives in Section 4. Any employee who becomes aware of an event that may require a declaration must notify the BCP Coordinator immediately.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. ALTERNATE SITE AND REMOTE OPERATIONS > 3.1 Alternate Site
chunks.text: The Firm's alternate site is a dedicated work-area recovery suite of 12 seats operated by Halvern Recovery Services, LLC in Bloomington, Minnesota. The suite is contracted for the Firm's exclusive use upon declaration and is available for occupancy within four hours of the Firm's notice of declaration. Each seat is equipped with a workstation configured to the Firm's standard image, dual monitors and telephone service capable of receiving forwarded calls from the Firm's main line. The BCP Coordinator maintains the list of personnel assigned to the alternate site, who include trading, operations, bill payment and technology staff.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. ALTERNATE SITE AND REMOTE OPERATIONS > 3.2 Remote Operations
chunks.text: All employees are issued Firm laptops and can work remotely through the Firm's secure remote access service, which requires multi-factor authentication. Remote operation is the primary recovery strategy for personnel not assigned to the alternate site. Bill payment and wire approvals performed remotely remain subject to the callback and dual approval controls in the Compliance Manual.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. ALTERNATE SITE AND REMOTE OPERATIONS > 3.3 Trust Company Operations
chunks.text: QHTC's office at 101 South Phillips Avenue, Suite 610, Sioux Falls, South Dakota serves as a secondary location for trust administration and for approval of trust distributions. If the Minneapolis area is affected, QHTC staff in Sioux Falls may process urgent distributions from trust accounts under QHTC's own plan, and the Firm's Relationship Leads coordinate with them by telephone and secure email.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. RECOVERY OBJECTIVES > 4.1 System Tiers and Objectives
chunks.text: Each system is assigned to a tier according to the effect of its loss on client obligations. Tier 1 systems carry a recovery time objective of four hours and a recovery point objective of one hour. Tier 2 systems carry a recovery time objective of 24 hours and a recovery point objective of 24 hours. Tier 3 systems carry a recovery time objective of five business days and a recovery point objective of 24 hours. | Tier | Systems | Recovery time objective | Recovery point objective | |---|---|---|---| | Tier 1 | Custodian portals and trading platforms, order management system, email, remote access, bill payment platform | 4 hours | 1 hour | | Tier 2 | Portfolio accounting and reporting platform, compliance system, document management, customer relationship management | 24 hours | 24 hours | | Tier 3 | Internal file shares for non-client matters, marketing systems, intranet | 5 business days | 24 hours |

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. RECOVERY OBJECTIVES > 4.2 Priority of Functions
chunks.text: After a declaration, functions are restored in the following order: (1) protection of personnel; (2) safeguarding of client assets, including heightened review of disbursements; (3) processing of time-sensitive payments, capital calls and trades; (4) communication with families; and (5) reporting and other functions.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. DATA BACKUP AND CRITICAL VENDORS > 5.1 Data Backup
chunks.text: Ferncastle Data Vault, Inc. performs the Firm's offsite data backups. Incremental backups of the Firm's file servers, document management system and locally hosted applications are performed every hour, and a full backup is performed each week. Backup copies are replicated to Ferncastle facilities in Omaha, Nebraska and Columbus, Ohio and are immutable for 90 days, so that they cannot be altered or deleted by a person who gains access to Firm systems. Email, messages and collaboration content are also retained by Arcwell Archive Services, Inc. Software-as-a-service applications, including the custodian portals and the reporting platform, are backed up by their providers under contractual commitments reviewed annually by the Director of Technology and Information Security.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. DATA BACKUP AND CRITICAL VENDORS > 5.2 Critical Vendors
chunks.text: | Vendor | Service | |---|---| | Norrell Bay Trust & Custody, N.A. | Qualified custodian; trading and cash movement | | Corvedale Clay Securities, LLC | Custodian for securities-based lending and option accounts | | Wexcombe Data Systems, Inc. | Portfolio accounting and client reporting | | Ostrander Valuation Data, Inc. | Primary pricing | | Pellow Stack IT, LLC | Managed information technology services | | Northgale Security Operations, Inc. | Security monitoring, detection and response | | Ferncastle Data Vault, Inc. | Offsite data backup | | Arcwell Archive Services, Inc. | Email and message archiving | | Halvern Recovery Services, LLC | Work-area recovery site |

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. DATA BACKUP AND CRITICAL VENDORS > 5.3 Vendor Continuity Due Diligence
chunks.text: The BCP Coordinator obtains from each critical vendor, at engagement and annually thereafter, a summary of its business continuity arrangements and the results of its most recent recovery exercise. For custodians, the Firm maintains contacts for each custodian's service team and secondary operations center, and a written procedure for placing instructions by telephone with callback verification if electronic platforms are unavailable.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.1 Frequency
chunks.text: The Plan is tested through a full-scale exercise at least annually, which includes relocation of designated personnel to the alternate site and restoration of Tier 1 systems from backup, and through tabletop exercises at least semi-annually. The communication tree in Section 7 is tested quarterly by an unannounced notification to all employees, and the time to obtain responses is recorded.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.2 Most Recent Tests
chunks.text: The most recent full-scale test was conducted on November 14, 2025. Designated personnel occupied the alternate site, and all Tier 1 systems were restored and available within 3 hours and 10 minutes of the simulated declaration. One deficiency was identified: printers at the alternate site had not been mapped to the Firm's standard image. It was remediated by Pellow Stack IT, LLC by December 5, 2025. The most recent tabletop exercise was conducted on March 19, 2026 and addressed a ransomware scenario affecting the Firm's file servers, including decision-making on restoration from immutable backups and communication with families.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.3 Reporting of Results
chunks.text: The BCP Coordinator prepares a written report of each full-scale and tabletop exercise, including deficiencies and remediation, which is delivered to the Management Committee and the Chief Compliance Officer.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. COMMUNICATION TREE > 7.1 Internal Notification
chunks.text: Upon a declaration, the Managing Partner or her delegate notifies the BCP Coordinator, who activates the Firm's mass notification service to send voice and text messages to all employees. The BCP Coordinator notifies the department heads (the Chief Investment Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief Compliance Officer, the Director of Technology and Information Security and the President of QHTC), each of whom confirms the status of every employee in the department and reports to the BCP Coordinator within two hours. Employees who cannot be reached are contacted at secondary numbers and emergency contacts recorded in the contact list.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. COMMUNICATION TREE > 7.2 Clients
chunks.text: A recorded message describing the disruption and alternative contact methods is placed on the Firm's main telephone line within two hours of declaration. Relationship Leads contact the primary contact of each Family Relationship within one business day of declaration, and immediately for any family with a pending wire, capital call or trade. Families are reminded that the Firm will never change payment instructions by email.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. COMMUNICATION TREE > 7.3 Custodians, Regulators and Counterparties
chunks.text: The Director of Operations notifies Norrell Bay and Corvedale Clay of the declaration and of any change in authorized contacts. The Chief Compliance Officer determines whether notice to the Securities and Exchange Commission or any other regulator is required, and coordinates with QHTC regarding notice to the South Dakota Division of Banking.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. PANDEMIC AND CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 8.1 Pandemic and Public Health Events
chunks.text: In a pandemic or other public health event, the Firm will shift to remote operations under Section 3.2, divide trading, operations and bill payment staff into separate teams that do not share office space, and cross-train personnel so that each critical function can be performed by at least two employees. The BCP Coordinator monitors public health guidance and determines, with the Managing Partner, when the office reopens.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. PANDEMIC AND CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 8.2 Cyber Incident Response
chunks.text: A cyber incident is managed under the incident response procedures in Section 11.6 of the Compliance Manual, with the Director of Technology and Information Security as Incident Response Lead. If the incident impairs operations, the BCP Coordinator may declare a business disruption. Northgale Security Operations, Inc. performs containment and forensic investigation. Vellacott Pryor LLP serves as the Firm's outside breach counsel and advises on privilege, notification obligations and communications. The Chief Financial Officer notifies the Firm's cyber liability insurer through the insurer's incident reporting line. Restoration of affected systems from backup begins only after Northgale confirms that the threat has been contained, so that restored systems are not reinfected.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. PANDEMIC AND CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 8.3 Fraudulent Disbursement Attempts
chunks.text: If there is reason to believe that an email account or client instruction has been compromised, the Director of Operations asks Norrell Bay and Corvedale Clay to apply heightened review to all disbursements from affected accounts, suspends processing of new third-party payment instructions until they are confirmed by callback, and notifies the Chief Compliance Officer. Any disbursement already sent is reported to the custodian and the receiving bank for recall.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated April 21, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. PLAN MAINTENANCE > SECTION 9. PLAN MAINTENANCE
chunks.text: The BCP Coordinator reviews the contact lists quarterly and the Plan as a whole annually, and updates the Plan upon any change in office location, alternate site, system tier or critical vendor. Each employee receives a copy of the Plan's employee procedures and wallet card upon hire and upon each revision.
