chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. SCOPE > 1.1 Applicability
chunks.text: This Schedule sets out the fees charged by Quenby Holt Family Office, LLC (the "Firm") under its investment management agreements and by Quenby Holt Trust Company ("QHTC") for trustee services. It forms part of each agreement. Where an agreement provides otherwise, the agreement controls.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. SCOPE > 1.2 Definitions
chunks.text: "Family Relationship" means all accounts of a client family aggregated under a single investment management agreement. "Reporting-only assets" means assets included in consolidated reporting over which the Firm has no management authority.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. ADVISORY FEE > 2.1 Tiered Rates
chunks.text: The annual advisory fee is calculated on the aggregate value of Family Relationship assets under management, applying each rate only to the portion of assets within its tier: | Family Relationship assets | Annual rate | |---|---| | First $25,000,000 | 0.80% | | Above $25,000,000 to $50,000,000 | 0.60% | | Above $50,000,000 to $100,000,000 | 0.45% | | Above $100,000,000 to $250,000,000 | 0.30% | | Above $250,000,000 | 0.20% | The first breakpoint occurs at $25,000,000. Family Relationship assets in excess of $250,000,000 are charged at 0.20% per year.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. ADVISORY FEE > 2.2 Illustration
chunks.text: A Family Relationship with $80,000,000 of assets under management pays an annual advisory fee of $485,000, calculated as $200,000 on the first $25,000,000, $150,000 on the next $25,000,000 and $135,000 on the remaining $30,000,000, an effective rate of approximately 0.61%.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. ADVISORY FEE > 2.3 Reporting-Only Assets
chunks.text: Reporting-only assets are charged at an annual rate of 0.05% of their reported value. They are not aggregated with assets under management for purposes of determining the tier rates in Section 2.1.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. ADVISORY FEE > 2.4 Fee Base
chunks.text: The fee base includes all assets under management in the Family Relationship, including cash and cash equivalents and assets of trusts for which QHTC serves as trustee. Interests in private funds, co-investments and other private investments are included at their values determined under the Firm's Valuation Policy. Unfunded capital commitments are excluded from the fee base. Margin balances and securities-based loans are not deducted.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. TRUST COMPANY FEES > 3.1 Full Trustee
chunks.text: Where Quenby Holt Trust Company serves as full trustee, it charges an annual fee of 0.10% of trust assets, subject to a minimum of $10,000 per trust per year.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. TRUST COMPANY FEES > 3.2 Directed Trustee
chunks.text: Where QHTC serves as directed trustee, acting at the direction of an investment adviser or distribution adviser named in the trust instrument, it charges a flat annual fee of $6,000 per trust.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. TRUST COMPANY FEES > 3.3 Billing of Trust Company Fees
chunks.text: Trust Company fees are calculated on the value of trust assets on the last business day of each calendar quarter, billed quarterly in arrears by QHTC and charged to the trust account. Extraordinary services, including trust decanting, migration of situs, litigation and administration of non-marketable assets outside the Firm's management, are charged at QHTC's hourly rates disclosed at the time of engagement.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. MINIMUMS AND SUPPLEMENTAL SERVICES > 4.1 Minimum Annual Fee
chunks.text: The minimum annual advisory fee is $150,000 per Family Relationship. The minimum does not include Trust Company fees or supplemental service fees.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.1 Billing Frequency and Basis
chunks.text: The advisory fee is billed quarterly in advance, at one-quarter of the annual fee, based on the aggregate market value of the Family Relationship on the last business day of the preceding calendar quarter. The fee for a partial first quarter is prorated by the number of days remaining in the quarter. Additions or withdrawals exceeding $2,000,000 in a single account during a quarter result in a prorated adjustment on the next invoice.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.2 Payment
chunks.text: Fees are deducted from the custodial accounts designated in the client's written authorization or, at the client's election, invoiced and payable within 30 days of the invoice date.

chunks.label: Schedule of Fees, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. BILLING, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.3 Termination and Refunds
chunks.text: Either party may terminate the investment management agreement on 30 days' written notice. Fees are prorated to the effective date of termination, and unearned fees paid in advance are refunded to the client on a pro rata basis within 30 days after the effective date of termination. A client may terminate within five business days after signing the agreement and receive a full refund. No termination fee is charged.

chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND EFFECT > SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND EFFECT
chunks.text: This memorandum, issued by the Chief Compliance Officer on September 8, 2026, records six amendments to the Firm's policies and procedures. The amendments in Sections 2 through 6 were approved by the Management Committee on September 3, 2026, following the mid-year compliance review. The amendment in Section 7 was approved by the Management Committee on June 9, 2026 and is recorded here so that all amendments since the last restatement appear in one place. The documents affected are the Compliance Manual (Version 2026.1, effective January 15, 2026), the Valuation Policy (Version 4.0, adopted February 10, 2026), the Business Continuity Plan (revised April 21, 2026) and the Schedule of Fees (effective January 1, 2026). Those documents are not being reissued at this time. Each amendment below supersedes the cited provision to the extent inconsistent with it, and this memorandum controls until the affected documents are restated. Unless otherwise stated, each amendment is effective on the date of this memorandum.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Policies and Procedures, dated September 8, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. PERSONAL TRADING DE MINIMIS EXEMPTION > SECTION 2. PERSONAL TRADING DE MINIMIS EXEMPTION
chunks.text: **Amends:** Compliance Manual, Section 4.3 (De Minimis Exemption). The aggregate amount below which transactions in an issuer with a market capitalization of at least $10 billion are exempt from pre-clearance is reduced from $25,000 to $10,000 in any 30 calendar day period. All other conditions of Section 4.3 are unchanged. Transactions above $10,000 in the aggregate in any 30 calendar day period require pre-clearance under Section 4.2. This amendment supersedes Compliance Manual Section 4.3.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Policies and Procedures, dated September 8, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. QUARTERLY TRANSACTION REPORT DEADLINE > SECTION 3. QUARTERLY TRANSACTION REPORT DEADLINE
chunks.text: **Amends:** Compliance Manual, Section 4.6 (Holdings and Transaction Reports). Quarterly transaction reports, and confirmations of the completeness of electronic data feeds, must be submitted no later than 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter, rather than 30 days. The amendment applies beginning with reports for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, which are due October 15, 2026. The deadlines for initial and annual holdings reports are unchanged. This amendment supersedes the corresponding deadline in Compliance Manual Section 4.6.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Policies and Procedures, dated September 8, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. VALUATION COMMITTEE MEETING FREQUENCY > SECTION 4. VALUATION COMMITTEE MEETING FREQUENCY
chunks.text: **Amends:** Valuation Policy, Section 2.3 (Meetings). The Valuation Committee will meet monthly, within 10 business days after the end of each calendar month, rather than quarterly. The change reflects the growth in private investments held by client families and the monthly valuation reports now delivered to families through the reporting portal. At each monthly meeting the Committee will approve valuations of Level 3 positions as of the month end and review the reports described in Sections 5 through 7 of the Valuation Policy. The first monthly meeting will be held within 10 business days after September 30, 2026. Special meetings may still be called as provided in Section 2.3. This amendment supersedes the meeting frequency stated in Valuation Policy Section 2.3.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Policies and Procedures, dated September 8, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. APPROVAL OF PRICE OVERRIDES > SECTION 5. APPROVAL OF PRICE OVERRIDES
chunks.text: **Amends:** Valuation Policy, Section 5.3 (Overrides). Any override of a price supplied by a pricing source must be approved in advance, in writing, by two voting members of the Valuation Committee, one of whom must be the Chief Financial Officer. The Chief Investment Officer may no longer approve overrides, because the Chief Investment Officer is responsible for the investment decisions whose results the valuations measure. The requirement for a written recommendation from the Controller, and the override log in Section 5.4, are unchanged. This amendment supersedes the approval requirement in Valuation Policy Section 5.3.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Policies and Procedures, dated September 8, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. OFFSITE DATA BACKUP VENDOR > SECTION 6. OFFSITE DATA BACKUP VENDOR
chunks.text: **Amends:** Business Continuity Plan, Section 5.1 (Data Backup) and Section 5.2 (Critical Vendors).
